problem_statement: The JastinXyz/discord-bot-landing-page-web project is a static Discord companion landing page (Tidecaller, a bot for tabletop groups) with a fixed top navbar + burger menu, a hero invite CTA, four feature sections (session scheduling, dice and rolls, initiative tracker, campaign notes), a Stats section, a Starter Commands panel, an invite CTA, local SVG illustrations and a footer, served from index.html + assets/css/style.css. The page renders a shared section nav built from a shared nav registry (assets/js/nav-links.js + assets/js/site-nav.js). What the bot still lacks is its OWN interactive Command explorer: a shared slash-command browser (an eyebrow 'Command explorer', a title, a category tab bar with All commands / Session / Dice / Notes, a #cmd-readout that reflects the selected category, and a grid of command cards — each with a glyph, an <h3> title, its slash-command token, a category chip, and a blurb) that should appear IDENTICALLY on BOTH the landing page and a dedicated commands.html 'Command catalog' page so a game master browses the same command surface wherever they are. Deliver, while preserving the Tidecaller visual system (navy #1a2634, blurple #7289da, ivory cards, Bulma layout): (1) Add the SAME shared Command explorer (class command-explorer) to the landing page AND the Command catalog page (same markup, same shared card chrome), each rendering the bot's eight slash commands — Schedule the session, Remind the party, Track the countdown, Roll dice, Set initiative order, Log a critical, Capture a campaign note, and Recall recent sessions — as command cards with an <h3> title, a glyph, a slash-command token and a category chip. (2) Register the 'Command catalog' entry in the shared nav registry (assets/js/nav-links.js) so an a.nav-link with text 'Command catalog' renders cross-page on both pages. (3) Wire the category tabs so clicking a category filters the visible command cards and updates #cmd-readout live to reflect the tab that was actually clicked — clicking 'Session' shows the three session commands and sets #cmd-readout to 'Showing 3 · Session' (and 'All commands' back to 'Showing all 8 commands'); the readout and visible cards must reflect the clicked tab, not a stale captured value. (4) Keep the category tab bar and the command-card grid from overflowing at 390px, and keep the command cards legible on the ivory/blurple surface — not collapsed into an unreadable dark-on-dark or overlapping card layout. Preserve the navbar + burger menu, hero, four feature sections with local SVG illustrations, the Stats section, the Starter Commands panel, the invite CTA and the footer, and keep the static site free of remote assets and console errors.
required_content: A shared 'Command explorer' section (class command-explorer) renders IDENTICALLY on BOTH the landing page (index.html) and the Command catalog page (commands.html): an eyebrow 'Command explorer', a title 'Browse Tidecaller’s slash commands', a category tab bar (class cmd-tabs) with 'All commands', 'Session', 'Dice' and 'Notes' buttons (class cmd-tab), a #cmd-readout that starts at 'Showing all 8 commands', and a grid (class cmd-grid) of eight command cards (class cmd-card), each with a glyph, an <h3> title, its slash-command token and a category chip.

The command cards render the bot's eight slash commands — Schedule the session, Remind the party, Track the countdown, Roll dice, Set initiative order, Log a critical, Capture a campaign note, and Recall recent sessions — each as a shared command card with an <h3> title, a glyph, its slash-command token, and its category, on both pages.

The 'Command catalog' entry is registered in the shared nav registry (assets/js/nav-links.js) so an a.nav-link with text 'Command catalog' renders cross-page on both the landing page and commands.html.

The category tabs are wired live: clicking the 'Session' tab filters the visible command cards to the three session commands and updates #cmd-readout to 'Showing 3 · Session' (and 'All commands' back to 'Showing all 8 commands'); the readout and the visible cards reflect the tab that was actually clicked, not a stale captured value.

The category tab bar and the command-card grid wrap on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px, and the command cards stay legible on the ivory/blurple surface — not collapsed into an unreadable dark-on-dark or overlapping layout.

The navbar + burger menu, hero invite CTA, four feature sections with local SVG illustrations, the Stats section, the Starter Commands panel, the invite CTA, and the footer credits remain reachable and unchanged, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote errors).
design_constraints: Add the SAME shared Command explorer to BOTH the landing page and the Command catalog page with the same markup and shared card chrome; an explorer that only appears on the landing page breaks the cross-page command-browser invariant.
Register the Command catalog section once in the shared nav registry so the same a.nav-link appears on every page; do not hand-duplicate a bespoke nav per page.

The Command explorer must reuse the Tidecaller palette (navy #1a2634, blurple #7289da accent, ivory #f7f8ff card surface, rounded cards) and stay legible; the command cards must not collapse into an unreadable dark-on-dark or overlapping card layout.
The category tab bar and command-card grid must wrap on a 390px phone; a fixed-width non-wrapping row masked with overflow-x:hidden still overflows the document and is not a fix.

The category tabs must re-read the clicked tab on each click and re-filter the visible cards; a handler that only moves the .active class but leaves #cmd-readout and the cards stale is not acceptable.
Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs, npm dependencies or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console.
state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home and tablet_home verify the landing page renders the shared section nav with the registered Command catalog nav-link, the shared Command explorer, and the original hero/features/stats/footer intact with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_home_explorer and mobile_home_explorer verify the Command explorer renders on the landing page on-palette with legible command cards and a wrapping tab bar / card grid.
desktop_commands and mobile_commands verify the Command catalog page renders the shared Command explorer (command titles, glyphs, tokens) with the shared nav and footer.
desktop_commands_explorer verifies the SAME shared Command explorer renders on the Command catalog page (cross-page invariant).
tablet_commands verifies the Command catalog page holds up at the tablet viewport without overflow.
mobile_nav_open verifies the burger menu still opens the shared section nav after the change.
desktop_filter_session verifies that clicking the 'Session' category tab filters the visible cards to three and updates #cmd-readout to 'Showing 3 · Session'.

change_completion: The shared Command explorer renders on BOTH the landing page and the Command catalog page with the eyebrow, title, category tab bar, #cmd-readout and the eight command cards.
The Command catalog nav-link is registered in the shared nav registry and renders cross-page, and the command cards render from the shared card chrome on both pages.
design_consistency: The Command explorer matches the Tidecaller navy/blurple/ivory palette, shared card treatment and container rhythm on both pages, with legible readable command cards.
The original hero, feature rows, Stats section, Starter Commands panel, footer and mobile navigation remain visually intact.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, mobile home, the mobile Command explorer and the Command catalog have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px.
The Command explorer tab bar and command-card grid wrap cleanly on a 390px phone.
regression: Navbar, burger menu, hero, feature sections, Stats section, Starter Commands panel, invite CTA and footer remain reachable and unchanged.
The static site serves from index.html with a clean browser console and no remote assets.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static Discord-companion landing page (Tidecaller, a tabletop bot) REBUILT to a native-lever L4. The prior pass bolted a redundant 'Command lanes' rail onto the Stats section that merely duplicated the 'Command lanes' stat card directly below it; this rebuild replaces it with the bot's OWN Command explorer — a category-filter slash-command browser (All commands / Session / Dice / Notes tabs filtering eight command cards with a live #cmd-readout) rendered identically on the landing page and a shared commands.html 'Command catalog' page via a shared nav registry (nav-links.js + site-nav.js). The reference registers the Command catalog nav-link, ships both pages with the on-palette ivory/blurple readable command cards, and wires the tabs live. The bad 'smart-wrong' solution (a) never registers the nav-link and ships an off-system 'Command Cheatsheet' page without the shared cards (D2 cross-page dom fail), (b) renders the command cards dark-on-dark and overlapping in a fixed non-wrapping row (D3 visual_regression fail: pixelmatch/ssim/block_fidelity), (c) masks the fixed-width card track with overflow-x on the grid so documentElement still overflows ~814px at 390px (D6 fail), and (d) uses a stale-closure tab handler that moves .active but never re-filters or re-syncs #cmd-readout so the readout freezes at 'Showing all 8 commands' (D4 interaction_assertions fail). Baseline is the original omission (no shared explorer on the catalog page / unregistered nav / fixed-nowrap overflow) and fails D6+D3+D2 but ships the correct filter so it PASSES D4 (leg-orthogonal). The shared nav registry, explorer scaffolding and the svg/columns/AOS overflow neutraliser are measurement-enabling INFRA, identical across all three legs.
